newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Quinn caps post budget spend at 13.01 bln punts.
newsitem.headline: Quinn caps post budget spend at 13.01 bln punts.

text.p: Irish finance minister Ruairi Quinn said on Monday that gross current expenditure after the 1997 budget would be no higher than 13.01 billion Irish pounds.
This represents an increase of 6.1 percent in nominal terms or 3.9 percent in real terms on 1996 levels.

"Gross current expenditure post-budget will be no higher than 13,014 million Irish pounds on the basis that no provision is made for any further increases in public service pay costs in 1997 beyond that already provided for in the Abridged Estimates," Quinn said in a statement.
The Budget Exchequer Capital allocation will be 1,574 million punts, all of which is allowed for in the Abridged Estimates, Quinn said.
He said the allocations in the Estimates largely reflect the cost of running existing policies and programmes in 1997.
"They provide for a continuation of the existing level of services run by departments in 1996 with some changes made by the government to reflect its policy priorities," Quinn said.
He said he considered this a prudent approach against the overall economic and budgetary background.
For 1996 the estimates showed the gross current expenditure outturn at 12,179 million punts and the gross capital expenditure total at 1,405 million punts.
The minister said additional Supplementary Estimates involving gross current expenditure of 89 million punts and gross capital expenditure of just under 73 million were being examined by parliament.
If these supplementary items were approved it would push the actual 1996 gross current spending up by 4.9 percent in nominal terms and 2.8 percent in real terms to 12,874 million punts.
Gross exchequer voted capital would increase by 6.5 percent in nominal terms and 3.6 percent in real terms to 1,574 million punts.
Quinn said the 1997 estimates reaffirm the government's commitment to tackling the unemployment problem, particularly long-term unemployment.
The Estimates also provide for an increase of 100 million punts in gross education expenditure and an expected 70 million punt increase over the expected 1996 outturn.
Gross current health spending will rise by 115 million punts in 1997 over the 1996 outturn, Quinn said.
